We've now settled the full set of behaviours across **saving, finding, and organising**, and explored the edge situations. Here's the scope in plain terms:

**What's settled (12 flows):**
- **Save** a link fast (one box, one click), with a quick review of the page's fetched title/description/preview/icon that you can correct; **duplicates** send you to the existing entry; **save-anyway** when a page's details can't be loaded; a gentle nudge on a non-address.
- **Find** by live, case-insensitive search across title, description, address, tags and notes — with **"quoted phrases"**, **and/or/not**, parentheses, and **#tag**.
- **Organise**: a **To read** reading list you can mark read; **Reference** (everything not to-read); **Archive**/restore; permanent **Delete** with a clear confirmation; freeform **tags** with autocomplete; **Markdown notes**; edit any field including the address.
- **Graceful states**: empty collection, empty views, no results, long text that wraps/clamps.

**One scope question before I propose building** — asked plainly, not technically:

Since you'll use this on both your **computer and phone**, your saved links need to live in **one shared place** both devices reach. Do you want it protected by a **personal sign-in** (so only you can get to your collection), or is it enough to keep it as just your own private copy with **no sign-in** for now?

Your answer decides whether a login is part of what I build. Once you've settled that, I'll ask for your go-ahead to **start implementing this scope**.
